study type: Secondary analysis of a randomised controlled trial
exposure: Variables known at labour induction (e.g., parity, height)
Variables describing the course of labour induction (e.g., amount of oxytocin stimulation)
cohort: The study included 1060 women with a cervical dilatation of 6 cm after oxytocin stimulation for induced labour.
finding: An AI model was developed that effectively predicted the individual risk of caesarean delivery in women undergoing induced labour, potentially assisting in tailored oxytocin management.
mod_finding: The AI model indicated that women delivering vaginally were more likely to be parous, taller, to have a lower estimated birth weight, and to be stimulated with a lower amount of oxytocin.
birth_weight: Estimated birth weight was a predictor in the AI model, with lower estimated birth weight associated with vaginal delivery.
